teams.heading: Fijian rugby forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies after training session in Japan
teams.body: The Fijian rugby community is mourning the sudden death of back-row forward Saimoni Vunilagi, who has passed away in Japan at the age of 26. Vunilagi’s second-division club, Kyushu KV, confirmed he died on Friday morning in a Fukuoka hospital after developing severe symptoms consistent with heatstroke following a team practice. The 196cm, 117kg forward had played in Japan since beginning his professional career in 2023. His club expressed their devastation, extending condolences to the family.

lead.why: The tragic passing of Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan is the most widely reported and significant news story today.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick awards five new England contracts while axing Elliot Daly
teams.body: England head coach Steve Borthwick has shaken up his squad, awarding five players their first enhanced Elite Player Squad contracts. Prop Asher Opoku-Fordjour, lock Alex Coles, flanker Guy Pepper, scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet, and centre Seb Atkinson have secured the £150,000 deals. Conversely, Elliot Daly and Ben Curry have been axed alongside Ollie Lawrence, Tom Roebuck, and France-bound Tom Willis. The hybrid deals give Borthwick final say over medical and conditioning matters as England build towards their autumn campaign.

lead.why: This represents a major selection and contract overhaul of the national squad by Steve Borthwick ahead of the upcoming season.

teams.heading: Kicking coach Vlok Cilliers joins Bulls after shock France departure
teams.body: Former France kicking coach Vlok Cilliers has joined the Bulls backroom staff following his sudden departure from Fabien Galthié's setup. The French Rugby Federation confirmed reports that Cilliers — who spent seven years sharpening the national side's tactical kicking and Thomas Ramos' goal-kicking — was relieved of his duties alongside defence specialist Shaun Edwards. Galthié reportedly instigated the shake-up to revitalise the squad ahead of the World Cup, prompting the 58-year-old Cilliers to return to Pretoria.

teams.heading: Former Ireland out-half Brian Smith has passed away aged 59
teams.body: The Irish rugby community is mourning the death of former dual-international playmaker Brian Smith, who has passed away aged 59. Capped nine times for Ireland at out-half during his studies at Oxford University, Smith also won six Test caps for Australia. The IRFU stated they were 'saddened to hear of the passing of former out-half Brian Smith following a short illness', paying tribute to a player and coach who excelled across both hemispheres.

lead.why: The rugby world is mourning the passing of former Ireland and Australia playmaker Brian Smith at the age of 59.

teams.heading: Tomás Albornoz remains suspended for upcoming Argentina matches against Australia
teams.body: Tomás Albornoz’s four-match suspension, handed down last week following his altercation with referee Angus Gardner after the defeat to England, remains ongoing. The ban rules the fly-half out of Argentina’s matches against South Africa and the upcoming double-header against Australia, as well as a fixture for his club Toulon. The disciplinary committee noted Albornoz had to be restrained by teammates after twice approaching Gardner, though he denied his behaviour was abusive or offensive.

teams.heading: Taniela Tupou scores twice as Wallabies crush Japan for third straight win
teams.body: The Wallabies secured their first three-match winning streak since 2024 with a clinical 56-17 victory over Japan in Townsville. After leading 21-17 at the interval, Les Kiss’s side scored 35 unanswered points in the second half, crossing for eight tries in total. Prop Taniela Tupou bagged a brace, while fly-half Carter Gordon impressed on his return from a calf injury. Kiss noted the squad found "balance in the selection" after making eight changes to the side that narrowly defeated the Brave Blossoms in Osaka last week.

lead.why: Australia's dominant eight-try victory and first three-match winning streak since 2024 is the day's primary story.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones' Japan collapses in Townsville as Australia secure dominant 56-17 win
teams.body: Japan suffered a heavy 56-17 defeat to Australia on Saturday after a competitive opening period in Townsville crumbled into a second-half rout. Despite leading 17-14 following tries from Harry Hockings, Naoto Saito, and Dylan Riley, the Brave Blossoms conceded 42 unanswered points. "The ball carrier is king, and then everyone else has got to follow after that," Jones noted regarding his use of geese videos, yet his side finished with 14 men after Harada's yellow card.

teams.heading: Caleb Clarke ruled out of South Africa tour following shoulder surgery requirement
teams.body: All Blacks wing Caleb Clarke is returning home from South Africa after scans confirmed a ruptured shoulder tendon sustained during Tuesday’s victory over the Sharks. The 27-year-old requires surgery, making him the second backline casualty of the tour following Billy Proctor’s earlier exit. While Richie Mo’unga has joined the squad as cover, Dave Rennie is yet to summon a replacement for Clarke, noting that "the side we are playing against the Bulls will be quite different to the first Test team."

lead.why: The injury to Caleb Clarke is a major squad setback that impacts selection for the upcoming Springboks series and reduces backline depth.

teams.heading: Josh Kronfeld labels Tony Brown the biggest danger to the All Blacks
teams.body: All Blacks legend Josh Kronfeld believes attack coach Tony Brown is the most significant threat to New Zealand in the upcoming four-Test series. Kronfeld argued that Brown’s influence prevents the Springboks from retreating into a conservative shell under pressure, providing the "danger factor" required to maintain an expansive game. While the world champions remain top of the log, Kronfeld warned that Rassie Erasmus’ side now possesses "way more dynamics" than previous eras, making it harder for opponents to exploit their traditional reliance on set-piece and kicking.

lead.why: Kronfeld's identification of Tony Brown as the primary tactical threat highlights the Boks' successful evolution into a more dynamic side.
